answer_box.title: Web Scraping with Ruby - The Complete Guide
answer_box.answer: Ruby has a mature scraping ecosystem: use Nokogiri for parsing HTML/XML, HTTParty or Faraday for HTTP, and Mechanize or Ferrum/Cuprite for stateful, JavaScript-heavy sites driven through a headless Chrome.
answer_box.snippet: Nokogiri parses the DOM, Mechanize keeps cookies and sessions, and Ferrum drives a real Chrome over CDP when the page needs JavaScript to render.

knowledge_graph.title: Ruby
knowledge_graph.description: Ruby is an interpreted, high-level, general-purpose programming language which supports multiple programming paradigms. It was designed with an emphasis on programming productivity and simplicity.

organic_results.snippet: In this tutorial you will learn how to scrape the web with Ruby, parse HTML with Nokogiri, follow links with Mechanize, and render JavaScript pages with Ferrum and a headless browser.

organic_results.title: Mechanize - RubyGems.org
organic_results.snippet: The Mechanize library is used for automating interaction with websites. Mechanize automatically stores and sends cookies, follows redirects, and can follow links and submit forms.

organic_results.title: How do I scrape a JavaScript-rendered page in Ruby? - Stack Overflow
organic_results.snippet: If the content is rendered by JavaScript, plain HTTParty plus Nokogiri will not see it. Use a headless browser driver such as Ferrum, Cuprite, or Selenium to let Chrome execute the scripts first.

organic_results.snippet: Makes HTTP fun again! HTTParty is a Ruby gem that provides a clean DSL for consuming REST services, with automatic parsing of JSON and XML responses into Ruby data structures.

related_questions.question: Is Ruby good for web scraping?
related_questions.answer: Yes. Ruby has Nokogiri for parsing, Mechanize for stateful navigation, and Ferrum/Cuprite for JavaScript-heavy pages, which together cover most scraping needs.

related_questions.question: What is the best Ruby gem for web scraping?
related_questions.answer: Nokogiri is the standard for HTML/XML parsing; pair it with HTTParty or Faraday for requests, and Ferrum when you need a real browser.

related_questions.question: How do I scrape JavaScript pages in Ruby?
related_questions.answer: Use a headless browser driver such as Ferrum or Cuprite that controls Chrome over the DevTools Protocol so the JavaScript executes before you read the DOM.

related_questions.question: Is web scraping legal?
related_questions.answer: Scraping publicly available data is generally legal in the US, but terms of service, copyright, and rate limits still apply. Consult counsel for specific cases.
